Q01.reason: It excludes extraction of the needed inter-scale estimate from the published fixed-ambient Green–Tao iteration and from plain reblocking, but does not itself supply a smaller new sufficient estimate than the pre-existing recurrence/average frontier.

X01.reason: It proves that several natural bounded-step renormalization families are impossible and isolates an explicit lower-bound-compatible sufficient density-loss inequality with theta<1 whose proof would close E3-Q4-SERIES.

A02.reason: It gives a valid finite submultiplicativity counterexample and useful lower-bound constraints on strong multiplicative/power recurrences, but its surviving sufficient recurrence classes are not selected as the minimal promoted route after X01.

S03.reason: It confirms no scoped primary-source theorem currently supplies the needed sequence-level estimate; this validates the gap but does not tighten its mathematical statement.

V02.reason: It independently verifies the existing E3-B02 reverse implication and therefore closes E3-V-B02; it does not advance E3-Q4-SERIES.

promoted_result.statement: For a_n=r_4(2^n)/2^n, prove existence of fixed L>=1, c>0, n_0, and 0<theta<1 with a_{n+L} <= a_n(1-c a_n^theta) for all n>=n_0.
promoted_result.consequence: Then a_n=O(n^(-1/theta)), and because 1/theta>1 the extremal series converges.
promoted_result.claim_boundary: E3-X01 does not prove this inequality. It promotes it as a sufficient missing lemma after ruling out stronger naive bounded-step laws.

retained_supporting_boundaries: Plain interval localization/reblocking yields normalized monotonicity but no strict loss.
Fixed-step uniform fractional contraction is incompatible with known lower constructions.
Fixed-window averaged uniform fractional contraction is likewise excluded.
A02 additionally records failure of literal submultiplicativity and lower-bound constraints on strong diagonal power recurrences.
